name: Beyond Snack
tagline: Kerala banana chips made with a standardised, modern process
excerpt: Kerala banana-chip brand Beyond Snack won backing from Ashneer Grover and Aman Gupta on Shark Tank India Season 1 and later raised a Series A.
content:
Beyond Snack sells Kerala-style banana chips in several flavours, with a focus on consistent quality and hygiene. Founder Manas Madhu pitched it in the eighth episode of Shark Tank India, aired on 29 December 2021.

Ashneer Grover and Aman Gupta invested in the brand on the show. The exact amount and stake were not confirmed by an outlet we rely on, so we leave them out.

The company has grown fast since. In January 2025 it raised about ₹71.3 crore in a Series A led by 12 Flags Group, the fund set up by former Reckitt chief Rakesh Kapoor. Inc42's filing data shows revenue rising year on year in FY25, though losses widened as it expanded.

shark_tank.pitch_summary: Manas Madhu pitched banana chips made with a standardised process. Ashneer Grover and Aman Gupta invested.

faq.q: Did Beyond Snack get a deal on Shark Tank India?
faq.a: Yes. Ashneer Grover and Aman Gupta invested in Season 1, Episode 8.

faq.q: How much funding has Beyond Snack raised since?
faq.a: Its latest round was a $8.3 million (about ₹71.3 crore) Series A in January 2025.
Inc42's filing data shows total revenue of about ₹52.9 crore in FY25, with a net loss.

lessons: Our analysis: taking a familiar regional snack and standardising it can be more fundable than inventing a new product.
Our analysis: the show was a starting point; the bigger capital came from institutional investors once the brand had retail reach.
notes: Ask and deal terms (₹50 lakh for 2.5%) appear only on Wikipedia/blogs (Unstop), so amount/equity/ask are left out. City given as Kerala (Inc42: 'Kerala-headquartered'); blogs name Alappuzha/Mavelikara. Inc42 converts the Series A to about INR 71.3 Cr.
